name: Generate Knowledge Documentation
description: Pipeline 2: LLM-powered knowledge synthesis. Reads metrics from pipeline 1, identifies cross-session patterns, and produces structured encyclopedia articles. The LLM enriches but never fabricates data — all referenced metrics come from deterministic pipeline 1 output.

inputs.name: Scope
inputs.description: Documentation scope: 'user' writes to content/user/docs/knowledge/, 'system' writes to content/system/docs/

inputs.name: LLM Model
inputs.description: Model to use for knowledge synthesis. Falls back to session default.

outputs.name: Articles Created
outputs.description: Number of new knowledge articles created

outputs.name: Articles Deprecated
outputs.description: Number of articles marked as deprecated

nodes.description: Read metrics index and existing knowledge base
LLM identifies patterns, confirmations, and contradictions across metrics data

inputs.systemPrompt: You are a research analyst for an AI model encyclopedia. Your task is to identify patterns across experiment metrics. You MUST reference specific session IDs and exact metric values — never fabricate numbers. Output a JSON array of observations with: topic, category, confidence (low/medium/high), evidence (array of {sessionId, metric, value}), recommendation, and whether it confirms/contradicts/is-new relative to existing knowledge.

nodes.description: Process each identified observation into a knowledge article
Generate or update a knowledge article in standard format

inputs.systemPrompt: You are a technical writer for an AI research encyclopedia. Write a knowledge article in Markdown with YAML frontmatter. The frontmatter MUST include: topic, category, title, confidence, status, sources (array with sessionId, date, relevance), contradictions, lastUpdated, relatedArticles. The body MUST include sections: ## Observation clé, ## Evidence (with data table), ## Recommandation, ## Limites, ## Historique. Never invent metrics — only reference data provided in the input.

nodes.description: Save the article to the knowledge directory
